plan.name: Show which Gobra proofs ran out of time
plan.summary: Keep D-0144's 20-minute container backstop and gate-error outcome, and give Gobra a 19-minute-30-second --packageTimeout (1170s) to report within that cap; this deliberately reduces proof time without increasing the maximum wait, as F1 A decides. Mount a fresh writable report directory beside read-only /work, request -g, read stats.json after success, failure and timeout, clean up on every exit including cancellation, and classify both the exit-1 member timeout and exit-0 package timeout as errors; map reported member IDs to files and receiver-qualified Go names with go/ast, name the Package obligation 'package initialization' without inventing a declaration or file, and count completion only when all Viper members with hasBody=true have verified=true, summing their millisecond times and retaining completed failed proofs. Exclude bodiless members from completed and unfinished proof progress unless Gobra explicitly says they did not terminate, without assuming unverified leaves have zero time or that abstract/trusted flags override explicit timeout evidence; show every reported unfinished member and every completed member's time in timeout errors reaching the agent gate, its run log, the final-gate factory post and CI, and show completed members slowest first in ordinary feedback and receipts, with missing or unreadable reports leaving selected source members 'not reported', preserving actual timeout messages and never inventing an active proof or changing ordinary verification outcomes or evidence fingerprints. Preserve function/contract lists and Docker isolation, extend the existing Gobra parser and deadline tests, and extract the existing modeled MCP gate closure as modeledGateTool used by mcpCmd so its staging, verification and error logging are tested offline; acceptance tests embed the two unedited captures supplied in #946, including their sources, package initialization and the singular '1 member timed out' output, while a new integration-tagged regression in internal/verify uses the supplied 24-branch Branches fixture with the pinned image, overflow checking, 2 CPUs, a 40-second package limit and a 2-minute backstop to require Gobra's own timeout naming Branches before the backstop, failing rather than skipping missing prerequisites when run in CI's integration suite. Update SPEC.md with a citation to [#946's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-946.json) and docs/gate.md to explain the two limits and lost proof time, body and package-initialization semantics, fallback, diagnostic-only timings, supplied capture provenance and real-tool test command; the builder need not generate captures or add testdata files.

tests.name: TestGobra946CapturedReports

tests.name: TestGobra946BodylessReportsAreNotPending
tests.says: Bodiless Viper members with nonzero time neither block completion nor count as unfinished or timed proofs; explicit timeout messages still survive.

tests.name: TestGobra946PackageInitializationCanTimeOut
tests.says: A timeout of the real package-initialization obligation is named without inventing a source declaration, while completed Go members keep their measured times.

tests.name: TestGobra946RunCollectsStatistics
tests.says: The actual Docker boundary requests the inner deadline and writable statistics output, consumes it on success, failure and timeout, and cleans it up.

tests.name: TestGobra946BothTimeoutShapes
tests.says: The exact member and package timeout messages supplied in the issue remain gate errors at exit 1 and exit 0, with source-qualified unfinished members and honest missing-report fallback.

tests.name: TestGobra946BackstopNamesOnlySelectedSources
tests.says: A killed run names selected functions and distinct receivers as not reported, excludes explorer and test functions, and fabricates no completed timing.

tests.name: TestGobra946FinishedGateShowsMeasuredTimes
tests.says: Measured member times survive Go verification into feedback and CI receipts, slowest first, but do not alter evidence fingerprints or mutate the report.

tests.name: TestGobra946CIGateNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The real verify command reports the captured timeout as a gate error, naming Branches and completed timings, excluding the unselected Successors explorer and writing no receipt.

tests.name: TestGobra946AgentGateNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The modeled MCP gate returns captured unfinished-member and completion details as an error and retains them in the build gate-run log.

tests.name: TestGobra946FactoryPostNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The factory failed-build post retains captured unfinished-member and completion details obtained through Gobra, with no active-proof invention or failed-Code receipt.

usage.summary: Revised plan.json and acceptance tests to embed the supplied captures, handle package initialization and bodiless members, and preserve the agreed deadlines. Check 1 passed: all 10 acceptance tests fail against the base as required; repo/ remains unchanged.

answers.question: D-0144 currently gives the entire Gobra container run a 20-minute deadline. Which limit should #946 use so Gobra's own --packageTimeout can emit unfinished-member diagnostics and stats.json before the container backstop fires?
answers.says: Keep the container backstop at 20 minutes and set Gobra's package timeout to 19 minutes 30 seconds, reserving time within the existing cap for startup and reporting. This preserves the current maximum wait but gives Gobra less proof time; document that tradeoff in the ratified plan, SPEC.md and docs/gate.md.
